gap: No result ChatGPT got states the dimensional error over a 200 mm replacement part for the scanners in our six-pick table. Only the Revopoint MetroX has a sourced length term among them, giving 0.03 mm + 0.1 mm/m × 0.2 m = 0.05 mm, or 1.7 times its 0.03 mm single-frame figure. The makers' own spec pages for the Einstar VEGA and Einstar 2 give no accuracy figure at all.
standout_why: I compared against the cited 3dprinting.com/3d-scanners/ and 3dprinting.com/scanners/best-small-format-3d-scanners/. The first already uses accuracy + rate × length, but only for metrology-tier scanners: MetroX Pro gets 0.052 mm at 300 mm and MetroY Pro 0.08 mm at 1 m. It marks volumetric accuracy as 'Not stated' for INSPIRE 2, Seal, Seal Lite, Mole, POP 3 Plus, MINI 2, Ferret Pro, Raptor and Einstar VEGA, and it does not list the standard MetroX. The small-format page says error over a part's length is 'Not computable' because it has no per-metre terms. So the method is already on a cited rival. Only the MetroX figure and the point that the other picks publish no length term are new.
decides: This confirms the MetroX as the pick for mechanical or replacement parts where a printed part has to fit. It is the only scanner in our table whose error over part length can be worked out from a published term: 0.05 mm at 200 mm. The INSPIRE 2, Seal, Moose, Otter and VEGA publish only single-frame or point figures (0.01 to 0.05 mm). Those numbers describe one frame, not a stitched 200 mm part, so the table should label its accuracy column 'single frame' and should not rank those scanners against each other on fit accuracy. It does not change the budget or small-object picks.
